project_name.justification: The authoritative project name is Thelon. The text refers to the project as the Angilak Property, which Labrador Uranium Inc. is acquiring from ValOre Metals Corp. The document's metadata section explicitly lists 'Thelon Project'. The text states: 'LUR will acquire ValOre’s Angilak Property located in Nunavut Territory, Canada (the “Angilak Property”)'.

company_name.justification: The buyer is Labrador Uranium Inc. which intends to change its name to Latitude Uranium Inc. upon completion of the arrangement. 'In addition, at the LUR AGM, LUR will also seek approval from LUR shareholders to authorize LUR to change its name to “Latitude Uranium Inc.” (the “Name Change”), conditional upon completion of the Arrangement.'

ceo_buyer.justification: The second article confirms the appointment: 'John Jentz, CEO of Labrador Uranium stated, “We are pleased to announce the completion of the Angilak acquisition...'' The first article announced the intention: 'LUR is also pleased to announce that Mr. John Jentz is expected to join LUR as Chief Executive Officer and Director of the Company...'

interest_acquired_percent.justification: The buyer acquired all shares of the subsidiary that holds the property. 'LUR will acquire from ValOre all of the issued and outstanding common shares of VO Subco'. VO Subco was formed to hold the Angilak Property.

primary_commodity.justification: The press release headline describes the transaction as creating a 'Premier Canadian Uranium Company' and the text highlights the project's attributes: 'Assets like Angilak are few and far between, boasting both high uranium grades...'
